text:
Sam: Heads up — users hitting a weird failure when using the redwood-js-sdk in Next.js Edge middleware. fetch signatures don't match and headers get dropped in the SDK's request pipeline.
Mira: ugh, can you paste a minimal repro? which Next version?
Sam: Next 13.4.4, middleware.ts (edge). Example: we call client.generate(...) inside middleware and the SDK tries to do `new Headers(req.headers)` which ends up missing trace headers after the SDK attaches auth.
Ashley: That sounds like the Node vs edge fetch mismatch. Edge runtime's Request/Headers are immutable-ish in Next middleware and some libs assume Node Request/Headers shape.
Sam: repro snippets: ```ts
// middleware.ts
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-js-sdk'

export const middleware = async (req: Request) => {
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'ping' })
  return NextResponse.json({ ok: true })
}
```
Mira: SDK code we traced: it does `new Headers(ctx.req.headers)` then mutates. In Edge that can drop pseudo-headers. Also the SDK tries to import 'node-fetch' types/behaviour for retry logic.
Ben: quick workaround: create a tiny adapter in middleware to clone headers to a plain object and pass explicit headers to the SDK call: ```ts
const headers = {}
for (const [k, v] of req.headers) headers[k] = v
const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'ping', headers })
```
Sam: that works but it's a pain to document. Wanted a proper SDK fix so middleware users don't need to polyfill.
Ashley: two parts to fix in SDK: (1) runtime detection and not mutate Headers objects — build a header-merge util that returns a fresh Headers or plain object depending on env; (2) exports/types: Node-specific retry/undici imports must be behind conditional exports so ESM edge bundlers don't include them.
Mira: agreed. For exports, add conditional in package.json: ```json
"exports": {
  "./fetch-adapter": {
    "node": "./dist/fetch-adapter.node.js",
    "default": "./dist/fetch-adapter.edge.js"
  }
}
``` That allows bundlers to pick a lightweight edge adapter.
Ben: typings note — TS types currently declare RequestInit with Node-ish BodyInit. Edge TS needs lib.dom. Suggest overloads in index.d.ts: `export function createClient(options: ClientOptions & { runtime?: 'edge' | 'node' })` and adapt types for headers param to accept Record<string,string> | Headers.
Sam: Another gotcha: Next's edge bundler does static analysis on imports. Even if edge adapter exists, if top-level code does `import { someNodeThing } from 'undici'` it breaks. Must do dynamic import inside node-only path or have separate entry points.
Ashley: Proposed patch: move node-only logic into `if (isNode) { await import('./node-only.js') }` and ensure package exports point `import` -> `dist/edge.mjs`, `require` -> `dist/node.cjs`. Also add a tiny runtime check util: `const isEdge = !process?.versions?.node` but be careful in some RN/etc.
Mira: For the Headers mutation, new helper: `mergeHeaders(orig, extra) { if (typeof Headers !== 'undefined' && orig instanceof Headers) { const h = new Headers(); for (const [k,v] of orig) h.set(k,v); for (const k in extra) h.set(k, extra[k]); return h } return {...Object.fromEntries(orig), ...extra} }`
Sam: I pushed a draft PR with tests that run in node and a browser-like fetch via undici. CI-bot: CI started for branch fix/edge-headers-1824 — running tests. :eyes:
Ben: will add a small e2e in a Next middleware fixture. Also update README with a short section: "Edge runtime notes — if you get header drops, upgrade to >= 0.8.5 which contains adapter and types".
Mira: +1. Also add a migration snippet for users: `import { adaptForEdge } from 'redwood-js-sdk/edge-adapter'` for temporary opt-in until we fully roll.
Ashley: One more thing: document that Edge runtimes don't allow sync file reads, so do not call any fs-based token caching at module top-level. That was another failure mode we saw.
Sam: thanks all — will clean PR comments and request reviews from infra and devex. If anyone hits this early, the headers-clone workaround is the short-term fix.
CI-bot: Canary published redwood-js-sdk@0.8.5-canary.3 (edge adapters included)
Mira: testing now in our internal demo — looks cleaner. :thumbsup:
